title: Joule, Calorie, kWh, BTU, eV: One Chart, Every Energy Unit You'll Meet
h1: Energy units — joule, calorie, kWh, BTU and eV
description: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ = 860 kcal = 3412 BTU = 2.25 × 10²⁵ eV. Same energy, different disciplines' vocabularies.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

hero: Nine common energy units, one physical quantity. Rounding errors compound across conversions — do all math in joules, present in whatever the audience reads.
body: Every field kept its favourite energy unit. Physicists use joules and eV. Utilities bill in kWh. Food labels use kcal (calling it Calorie with a capital C). HVAC keeps BTU. Nutrition sometimes reverts to plain calorie. Nuclear engineering slips into eV even in macroscopic calcs.
Chocolate bar: 250 kcal = 1.05 MJ = 0.29 kWh. Home daily electricity: 30 kWh = 108 MJ. Gallon of gasoline: 33.7 kWh = 121 MJ = 115 000 BTU. 1 eV per particle × Avogadro ≈ 96 kJ/mol.

Raise 100 L water from 20 to 60 °C. Q = mcΔT = 100 × 4186 × 40 = 16.7 MJ = 4.65 kWh = 15 875 BTU = 4000 kcal. All four numbers describe the same job — utility bill vs equipment nameplate vs food-science reference just pick different names.
Work in joules. Present in the audience's unit.

faqs.q: Is 'Calorie' with a capital C the same as calorie?
faqs.a: No — food 'Calorie' is 1 kcal = 1000 physics calories. It's a permanent source of confusion in nutrition literature.

faqs.q: Why is eV used for macroscopic energy?
faqs.a: Convenient when scaling from single-particle physics — 1 eV/atom × N_A ≈ 96.5 kJ/mol.
